turns.doctor_question: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Nice to meet you too, Doc. Well, I guess what brings me in is... this memorial I'm planning for my brother. It’s just gotten a lot bigger than I meant it to. 

I’ve been spending most of my days working on it lately—chasing down specific songs, calling folks up, planning out these big displays and even trips. My wife is the one who really pushed me to come see you. She says I’ve completely pushed aside the garden, my walking group, and just about everything else I normally do. So, I suppose that's why I'm here.

symptom_reasoning.S040: The patient describes spending most of their days intensely focused on planning a large memorial, calling people, and organizing displays and trips, indicating a significant increase in goal-directed activity.

turns.doctor_question: How long ago did your brother die?
turns.patient_response: He passed away about two months ago. That's when I started working on his tribute, and I've been at it pretty much ever since.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself longing intensely for your brother or preoccupied with thoughts of him most of the day, nearly every day?
turns.patient_response: No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I miss him, sure... but I'm not just sitting around crying or longing for him all day. I'm mostly just focused on getting this memorial done right. I think about him when I'm working on it, but it's not like I'm overwhelmed by it every second of the day.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly denies sitting around crying or being overwhelmed by sadness all day.

turns.doctor_question: Since your brother died, have you had persistent difficulty accepting that he is gone?
turns.patient_response: No, I know he's gone. I've accepted that. I just want to make sure his memorial is exactly what he deserves. I'm not in denial about him being dead or anything like that.
